T0673.title: Purdue Model
T0673.definition: The Purdue Model is a reference architecture that separates industrial control environments into enterprise, operations, control, and field-device levels.
T0673.description: The model divides industrial environments into enterprise networks, an industrial demilitarized zone, manufacturing operations, control systems, and field devices to clarify data flows, trust boundaries, and control placement. It supports segmentation, jump access, industrial firewalls, and one-way transfer. Cloud and edge connectivity blur traditional levels, so implementations must reflect actual assets and communication paths.
T0673.usageExample: A plant used the Purdue Model to separate the business and control networks and placed proxies and audit systems in the industrial DMZ.

references.title: Guide to Industrial Control Systems Security - NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3
